request.question:
In the figure, DE||AC and DF||AE. Prove that BF/FE = BE/EC

Figure: Triangle ABC with vertex A at the top and base BC horizontal. Point D is on side AB. Points F and E are on the base BC, in the order B, F, E, C from left to right. Line segments are drawn connecting A to E, D to E, and D to F.

turn_plan.question:
In the figure, DE||AC and DF||AE. Prove that BF/FE = BE/EC

Figure: Triangle ABC with vertex A at the top and base BC horizontal. Point D is on side AB. Points F and E are on the base BC, in the order B, F, E, C from left to right. Line segments are drawn connecting A to E, D to E, and D to F.

qualitative_claims.claim: In triangle ABE, DF parallel AE implies BF/FE equals BD/DA
In triangle ABC, DE parallel AC implies BD/DA equals BE/EC
BF/FE equals BE/EC by transitivity through BD/DA

assumptions: ABC is a triangle with base BC
F and E lie on BC in order B-F-E-C

figure: point_figure
parts you may [FOCUS] (use each id exactly):
- A: point A
- B: point B
- C: point C
- D: point D
- F: point F
- E: point E
- AB: side AB
- BC: side BC
- CA: side CA
- AE: side AE
- DE: side DE
- DF: side DF
reveal groups you may [FOCUS]: g_setup, g_parallel
diagram.caption: Triangle ABC with D on AB and B-F-E-C on base, with DE parallel AC and DF parallel AE.

steps_sent.spoken_text: Look at this triangle figure, we want to prove a lovely ratio result about the segments on the base.
Look at this figure with triangle A B C and points D, F, E inside it.
Notice segment DE is parallel to side AC in our figure.
Follow segment DF which is parallel to segment AE .
Now look at the smaller triangle with vertex A and vertex B and E on the base.
By Basic Proportionality Theorem, a parallel line divides the two sides in the same ratio.
This is side AB where point D lies, part of the big triangle.
Follow the base BC up to point C to see the second division.
Notice point F and point E give the same middle ratio B D by D A, so the two outer ratios match.
